method: A shutter angle is the fraction of each frame for which the shutter is open, so the exposure time is the angle divided by 360 and by the frame rate: 180 degrees at 24 fps is 0.5 / 24 = 1/48 s, and 172.8 degrees at 24 fps is exactly 1/50 s, the usual setting for shooting under 50 Hz lighting. The calculator also solves the inverse, angle = 360 x shutter speed x frame rate, accepting a shutter speed in seconds or as a fraction such as 1/48. It reports the shutter speed as a fraction and in milliseconds, the frame interval, the percentage of each frame the shutter is open, and the exposure change in stops relative to a 180 degree shutter, plus a table of 45, 90, 144, 172.8, 180, 270 and 360 degrees at the entered rate. Frame rates are limited to 1-240 fps, angles to 1-360 degrees, and a shutter speed may not be longer than one frame interval. The conversion assumes the whole frame is exposed at once; rolling-shutter readout, lighting flicker, aperture and ND filtration are not modelled. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: American Cinematographer Manual, 10th ed., ASC Press (shutter angle and exposure time)
Exposure time = shutter angle / (360 x frames per second), the standard cinema-camera relation also stated in ARRI and RED camera manuals
